summary: The run built a functional Ironclad deck and successfully obtained both Act 2 keys, but its HP became the decisive constraint. The largest avoidable loss occurred in the Act 2 event, where repeated HP-cost choices reduced HP from 38 to 13 immediately before the Automaton fight. The final deck also became diluted by repeated additions, which likely reduced consistency, though the event damage is the clearest causal mistake.

lessons.title: Do not chain optional HP-loss event choices at low health
lessons.situation: When an event repeatedly offers rewards for losing HP, especially after choosing Coffee Dripper and while below comfortable health, reassess after each payment instead of pursuing multiple rewards.
lessons.lesson: After the first worthwhile event reward, leave rather than repeatedly paying HP for more rewards unless the gain is clearly necessary. Preserving enough HP to reach the next combat is more important than accumulating marginal gold or potion value.
evidence_points: At Act 2 Floor 31, HP fell from 38 to 32 after choosing the potion option, then from 32 to 26 after choosing the 90-gold option, then from 26 to 19 after choosing another potion option, and finally to 13 when leaving.
The next combat, the Automaton fight on Act 2 Floor 33, began with only 13/80 HP and ended with death.
lessons.reasoning: The event cost 25 HP in total and directly placed the run at 13 HP before the boss. The repeated choices were optional and created a much more fragile state than the preceding 38 HP would have caused.

lessons.title: Stop adding low-priority duplicate cards once the deck is already large
lessons.situation: When the deck is trending toward 30 or more cards and already has several copies of a role, skip rewards or prioritize only cards that solve a specific upcoming fight.
lessons.lesson: Prefer skipping repeated generic attacks or block cards once the deck has adequate coverage; preserve draw and consistency rather than continuing to add duplicates. In particular, do not keep taking Shrug It Off or Rage without a clear reason.
evidence_points: The final build had 33 cards, including four Shrug It Off copies in total, one upgraded, and two Rage copies.
The run continued taking or buying similar cards late: Shrug It Off at Act 2 Floor 22, Shrug It Off+ at Floor 25, and another Shrug It Off from the Floor 30 shop.
lessons.reasoning: The repeated additions increased deck size while duplicating effects already represented in the build. A smaller deck would make key defensive and scaling cards more likely to appear during difficult fights, although the trajectory does not prove this alone caused the loss.
